headline: Trump: Looking forward to meeting PM Tarique soon
summary: US President Donald Trump has written to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, expressing his desire for a direct meeting and thanking him for the decision to purchase Boeing aircraft.
details: US President Donald Trump has expressed his hope for a direct meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in a letter written to the leader.
In the letter, Trump thanked the Prime Minister for the decision to purchase Boeing aircraft, stating that 'Boeing will not let you down, and I will not forget.'
The communication highlights a strengthening of ties between the US and Bangladesh, focusing on both diplomatic relations and commercial interests.
The letter serves as a marker of diplomatic engagement between the two nations' leaders as they look toward future cooperation.

topic: nid and call records sold online
headline_marked: Tk 500 and 17 minutes: [[NID data being sold online]]
headline: Tk 500 and 17 minutes: NID data being sold online
summary: An investigation by Dismislab reveals a thriving online market for sensitive personal data, including NIDs, call records, and location data.
details: A digital media research initiative, Dismislab, has uncovered an online market where citizens' personal data is being sold via Facebook, Telegram, WhatsApp, and dedicated websites.
The available data includes National Identity Cards (NIDs), call detail records (CDRs), mobile phone location data, SMS lists, tax identification numbers (TINs), and passport information.
In a test purchase, researchers paid Tk 500 and received a PDF of a subscriber's NID card within 17 minutes, with all details matching the SIM card owner.
The investigation identified 10 active websites and over 600 Facebook advertisements in a single month, with at least 112 different mobile numbers used for contact.
Call detail records (CDRs) were also sold, with one request for three months of records for a Grameenphone number costing Tk 1,050 and delivered within 2.5 hours.
Mobile tower-based location data, including a Google Maps link, was provided within 16 minutes of payment at another website.
Some sellers claim to use an API to breach government servers to collect this data, though Dismislab could not independently verify this specific claim.
Experts warn that CDRs and location data can be used to track a person's patterns of movement and identify their contacts.
caption:
Your NID, call records, and live location could be for sale for as little as Tk 500. A new investigation reveals a dangerous breach of personal privacy.

A digital media research initiative, Dismislab, has uncovered an online market where citizens' personal data is being sold via Facebook, Telegram, WhatsApp, and dedicated websites.

The available data includes National Identity Cards (NIDs), call detail records (CDRs), mobile phone location data, SMS lists, tax identification numbers (TINs), and passport information.

In a test purchase, researchers paid Tk 500 and received a PDF of a subscriber's NID card within 17 minutes, with all details matching the SIM card owner.

The investigation identified 10 active websites and over 600 Facebook advertisements in a single month, with at least 112 different mobile numbers used for contact.

Call detail records (CDRs) were also sold, with one request for three months of records for a Grameenphone number costing Tk 1,050 and delivered within 2.5 hours.

Mobile tower-based location data, including a Google Maps link, was provided within 16 minutes of payment at another website.

Some sellers claim to use an API to breach government servers to collect this data, though Dismislab could not independently verify this specific claim.

Experts warn that CDRs and location data can be used to track a person's patterns of movement and identify their contacts.
